source_caption:
To make the film’s most deeply devastating emotional climax work, Tom Hanks had to completely shatter the audience’s understanding of his character. When Jenny finally introduces Forrest to his young son, Forrest physically backs away in sheer panic before asking his very first, breathless question: “Is he smart, or is he... like me?” In that single, profoundly heartbreaking line delivery, Hanks brilliantly reveals that despite his constant, childlike optimism throughout the entire movie, Forrest has always been painfully, entirely aware of his own intellectual limitations. By suddenly dropping the veil of blissful ignorance to show a father’s terrified vulnerability, Hanks masterfully proves that the most powerful cinematic moments often come from revealing the quiet, hidden pain a character has been secretly carrying the entire time.
⠀
Forrest Gump (1994), directed by Robert Zemeckis, starring Tom Hanks, Robin Wright, Gary Sinise. A deeply kind, incredibly optimistic Alabama man with a low IQ unwittingly influences some of the most profoundly defining historical moments of the 20th century, all while desperately yearning to reunite with his fiercely troubled childhood sweetheart.

source_details.synopsis: Forrest Gump is a 1994 American comedy-drama film directed by Robert Zemeckis. An adaptation of the 1986 novel of the same name by Winston Groom, the film's screenplay was written by Eric Roth. It stars Tom Hanks in the title role, alongside Robin Wright, Gary Sinise, Mykelti Williamson, and Sally Field in lead roles. The film follows the life of an Alabama man named Forrest Gump (Hanks) and his experiences in the 20th-century United States. Principal photography took place between August and December 1993, mainly in the tri-states Georgia, North Carolina, and South Carolina.
